data.name: Baked Salmon
data.description: Baked salmon is a simple, healthy Turkish-inspired dish where salmon fillets are seasoned, topped with lemon and herbs, then baked to tender perfection.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Place the salmon fillet on a baking tray lined with parchment paper or lightly oiled.
Drizzle olive oil over the salmon and season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of dried oregano.
Slice the lemon thinly and place the slices on top of the salmon.
Sprinkle chopped fresh parsley over the salmon.
Bake in the preheated oven for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Remove from the oven and let rest for a few minutes before serving.

data.name: Baked Salmon with Dill
data.description: A simple and healthy baked salmon dish flavored with fresh dill and optionally lemon, perfect for a quick nutritious meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius (400 degrees Fahrenheit).
Place the salmon fillets on a baking dish lined with parchment paper or lightly greased.
Season the salmon with salt and pepper to taste.
Sprinkle chopped fresh dill evenly over the salmon fillets.
Drizzle olive oil over the fillets to keep them moist during baking.
Optionally, add thin lemon slices on top of each fillet for extra flavor.
Bake in the preheated oven for 12-15 minutes, or until the salmon is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork.
Remove from oven and let rest for a couple of minutes before serving.
Serve the baked salmon garnished with extra fresh dill if desired.

data.name: Cedar Plank Smoked Salmon
data.description: Cedar plank smoked salmon is a flavorful dish where salmon is cooked on a soaked cedar plank, imparting a subtle smoky aroma with moist and tender results.
instructions: Soak a cedar plank in water for at least 1 hour to prevent it from burning during cooking.
Preheat the grill to medium heat, around 350°F (175°C).
Place the salmon fillet skin-side down on the soaked cedar plank.
Brush the salmon with olive oil to keep it moist during smoking.
Season the salmon with salt, pepper, and your choice of herbs such as dill and parsley.
Place the cedar plank with salmon directly on the grill grates.
Cover the grill and smoke the salmon for approximately 20-30 minutes until cooked through and flaky.
Remove the cedar plank from the grill carefully and let the salmon rest for a few minutes before serving.
Serve the smoked salmon with lemon wedges and garnish with additional fresh herbs if desired.

data.name: Choo Chee Curry with Salmon
data.description: Choo Chee Curry with Salmon is a rich and aromatic Thai red curry featuring creamy coconut milk and tender salmon, flavored with fragrant kaffir lime leaves and Thai basil.
instructions: Cut the salmon into bite-sized pieces and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add the choo chee curry paste and stir-fry for about 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer while stirring.
Add the fish sauce and palm sugar to the sauce and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the salmon pieces to the curry sauce and cook gently for 5-6 minutes until the salmon is just cooked through.
Add the kaffir lime leaves torn into pieces and stir to combine, then remove from heat.
Serve the choo chee salmon curry hot, garnished with Thai basil leaves and accompanied by steamed jasmine rice.

data.name: Eggs Benedict Smoked Salmon
data.description: Eggs Benedict with smoked salmon is a classic brunch dish featuring toasted english muffins topped with cream cheese, smoked salmon, perfectly poached eggs, and rich hollandaise sauce.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a gentle simmer and add a tablespoon of vinegar.
Crack each egg into a small bowl, then gently slide each egg into the simmering water to poach for about 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are soft.
Meanwhile, toast the english muffin halves until golden brown and set them on plates.
Spread a thin layer of cream cheese on each toasted muffin half.
Place smoked salmon slices evenly on top of the cream cheese on each muffin half.
Using a slotted spoon, remove the poached eggs from the water, letting excess water drain off, then carefully place one egg on top of the salmon on each muffin.
Prepare hollandaise sauce by whisking egg yolks, lemon juice, and melted butter over low heat until thickened, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Spoon warm hollandaise sauce generously over each poached egg.
Garnish with chopped fresh chives and a pinch of black pepper if desired.
Serve immediately while warm.

data.name: Farfalle with Salmon
data.description: Farfalle with Salmon is a simple and elegant Italian pasta dish featuring bowtie-shaped pasta tossed with tender salmon pieces in a creamy lemon-dill sauce.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, then add the farfalle pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente.
While the pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add chopped garlic to the skillet and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Cut the salmon into bite-sized pieces and add to the skillet, cooking gently until the salmon is opaque and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes.
Add heavy cream and lemon juice to the skillet, stirring to combine and simmering for 2-3 minutes until the sauce slightly thickens.
Drain the cooked pasta, reserving a small amount of pasta water.
Add the pasta to the skillet with the salmon sauce, tossing to coat.
If the sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water to loosen it.
Season with salt, pepper, and chopped dill, mixing well.
Serve the pasta garnished with extra dill and lemon zest if desired.

data.name: Gravlax Salmon (Cured Salmon)
data.description: Gravlax is a Nordic dish of raw salmon cured with a mixture of salt, sugar, and dill, resulting in a flavorful and delicate appetizer.
instructions: In a bowl, mix sugar, salt, crushed white pepper, and chopped dill together.
Lay a large piece of plastic wrap on a flat surface and spread half of the curing mixture evenly on it.
Place the salmon fillet skin-side down on the curing mixture.
Spread the remaining curing mixture evenly over the top of the salmon.
Wrap the salmon tightly with the plastic wrap, then place it in a shallow dish.
Place a weight on top of the wrapped salmon to press it down slightly.
Refrigerate the salmon for 48 hours, turning it over every 12 hours to ensure even curing.
After curing, remove the salmon from the wrap and gently rinse off the curing mixture under cold water.
Pat the salmon dry with paper towels.
Slice the gravlax thinly on a diagonal, and serve chilled with mustard sauce, rye bread, or crackers.

data.name: Grilled Salmon
data.description: Grilled salmon is a simple and flavorful dish where fresh salmon fillets are seasoned and char-grilled to perfection, offering a smoky taste and tender texture.
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Brush the salmon fillets with olive oil on both sides to prevent sticking.
Season the salmon with salt and black pepper to taste.
Place the salmon fillets skin-side down on the grill.
Grill the salmon for about 4-6 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until the fish flakes easily with a fork and has grill marks.
Remove the salmon from the grill and let it rest for a couple of minutes.
Garnish with fresh lemon slices and chopped parsley before serving.

data.name: Grilled Salmon Teriyaki
data.description: Grilled salmon teriyaki is a Japanese-inspired dish where salmon fillets are marinated and glazed with a sweet and savory teriyaki sauce, then perfectly grilled for a flavorful and healthy meal.
instructions: Prepare the teriyaki sauce by mixing soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and grated ginger in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Marinate the salmon fillets in half of the teriyaki sauce for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat and lightly oil the grill grates to prevent sticking.
Remove salmon from the marinade, letting excess drip off, and grill the fillets skin-side down first for about 4-5 minutes.
Flip the salmon carefully and grill the other side for an additional 3-4 minutes or until cooked through and slightly charred.
While grilling, heat the remaining teriyaki sauce in a small saucepan over medium heat and cook until it thickens into a glaze.
Brush the cooked salmon with the thickened teriyaki glaze and remove from the grill.
Serve the grilled salmon teriyaki garnished with chopped green onion and sesame seeds over steamed rice or your preferred side.

data.name: Grilled Salmon with Bearnaise Sauce
data.description: Grilled salmon served with classic French bearnaise sauce, a creamy and tangy herb-infused butter sauce made with egg yolks and tarragon.
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat and oil the grill grates to prevent sticking.
Season the salmon fillets with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place the salmon fillets on the grill, skin side down, and cook for about 4-5 minutes per side or until cooked through and slightly charred.
While the salmon is grilling, prepare the bearnaise sauce.
In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, white wine, chopped shallot, dried tarragon, and peppercorns.
Simmer the mixture over medium heat until reduced by half, then strain to remove solids and let cool slightly.
Fill a double boiler or a heatproof bowl set over simmering water with the reduction and add egg yolks.
Whisk continuously until the mixture thickens and becomes pale and fluffy.
Slowly drizzle in melted butter while whisking constantly to emulsify the sauce.
Stir in chopped fresh tarragon and season with salt and a pinch of cayenne pepper.
Serve the grilled salmon topped with generous spoonfuls of bearnaise sauce and garnish with fresh tarragon if desired.
